title: kubelet cgroupv2 throttle & disk I/O latency triage notes
body:
Summary:

This is an on-call triage note capturing investigation into a recurring class of node pressure incidents we observed across a subset of GPU-backed nodes (g5x.*) in eu-west-1 between 2024-03-20 02:00–08:00 UTC. Symptom was sustained high kubelet CPU wait and frequent pod eviction/oom_kill-like behavior, but dmesg/memory signals were inconsistent. Root cause signal points to aggressive cgroupv2 memory+io throttling triggered by a combination of containerd snapshotter disk stalls and kubelet cgroup accounting on cgroupv2-enabled kernels.

Why this is different from other node-pressure incidents:
- Not primarily kernel OOM nor kubelet OOM-handled memory exhaustion.
- Disk I/O stalls (block layer latency) cause processes inside system slices to block, which drives systemd/cgroupv2 throughput limits and elevated io.stat values, resulting in kubelet reporting long attach/detach/device timeouts and scheduling backoffs.
- Observed correlation with heavy image pull activity and ephemeral checkpointing from a model-serving workload that writes large mmap files during warmup.

Incident timeline (high level):
- 2024-03-20 02:03 UTC: First Pager — 3 nodes in eu-west-1 autoscaling group reported kubelet restart loop in monitoring.
- 02:07 UTC: On-call runs node-tail on kubelet logs; saw repeated messages: "detected high pod start latency: 2.1s attach/detach; device-plugin timeouts"
- 02:14 UTC: Containerd reported repeated syscall EIO in snapshotter plugin (overlayfs) and long fsync latencies (>2000ms) in logs.
- 02:25 UTC: Ops ran iostat and fio on a healthy spare node; baseline IO latencies <10ms. On impacted nodes, iostat showed avg await 1800ms, %util near 100 for nvme devices.
- 03:10 UTC: Temporary mitigation — cordon + drain of 5 most-affected nodes; restarted containerd and kubelet; some pods recreated on other nodes and the cluster stabilized.

Detection and evidence collected:
- kubelet logs (journalctl -u kubelet): repeated "Failed to kill podSandbox" and large "Pod start latency" warnings
- containerd logs (/var/log/containerd.log): overlayfs EIO and snapshotter retry loops
- dmesg: occasional "blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector ..." entries matching times of observed high latency
- iostat/sar/perf: sustained disk await >> 1000ms; NVMe SMART showed high media errors on two devices (nvme0n1p1) but SMART overall reported mostly nominal health; need follow-up to confirm hardware vs firmware flakiness
- cgroup counters (cgroupv2): io.stat showing heavy bytes and time in write and sync categories for system.slice/containerd.service and for kubelet.service

Key commands used during triage (copyable):
- journalctl -u kubelet -S "2024-03-20 01:50" -U "2024-03-20 03:30" --no-pager
- journalctl -u containerd -S "2024-03-20 01:50" -U "2024-03-20 03:30" --no-pager
- cat /proc/pressure/io  # check pressure stall information (PSI)
- cat /sys/fs/cgroup/io.stat  # cgroupv2 io accounting for relevant slices
- systemd-cgtop 1 1  # live observation of cgroup IO/CPU/memory usage
- iostat -x 1 10 /dev/nvme0n1
- smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1
- sudo /usr/local/bin/snapshot-debug.sh    # custom helper to dump overlay snapshot metadata (generated during incident)

Immediate mitigations attempted and outcome:
- Node cordon + drain: short-term, prevented more evictions but increased pressure on remaining nodes. Outcome: cluster stabilized after moving non-critical pods off impacted nodes.
- Restart containerd: cleared snapshotter retry loops on two nodes; after restart, containerd snapshotter latencies returned close to baseline but relapsed on one node (~40m later).
- Restart kubelet: removed stuck housekeeping goroutines, but not sufficient alone while disk latency persisted.
- Fallback to older snapshotter (built-in overlayfs writer) via hotfix config on one node: temporarily reduced EIO occurrences. This points to a regression in the overlay snapshot plugin/driver/firmware interaction.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
1) Heavy ephemeral writes from model warmup (large mmap and fsync) + image pulls saturate NVMe queues.
2) Under cgroupv2 accounting, system.slice/containerd and kubelet slices record huge io.stat time values; process-level ops spend large % time in uninterruptible sleep which kubelet interprets as pod start and eviction risk.
3) On some hardware (specific NVMe firmware), sustained high queue depths cause firmware-level stalls that return EIO transiently. This surfaces as occasional blk_update_request errors in dmesg and containerd snapshotter EIO errors.
4) Kubelet then cascades to scheduler backoff and cordoning due to perceived instability.

Why cgroupv2 matters here:
- cgroupv2 exposes different io.stat accounting that kubelet/systemd uses for throttling decisions; we saw kubelet controller manager heuristics reacting to high cgroup io time and lowering concurrency on the node, exacerbating pressure.

Gap analysis (what we don't know yet):
- Whether the NVMe returns are hardware-firmware defects or orchestrated by kernel driver interaction under very high simultaneous writes. Need vendor analysis.
- Exact threshold where snapshotter activity shifts from healthy to pathological.
- Whether a default kubelet config change (e.g., kube-reserved, eviction thresholds) can prevent cascade without hampering throughput for model-serving workloads.

Short-term action items (<=72h):
- Tag impacted host fleet (eu-west-1 g5x.*) and schedule proactive NVMe SMART dump and firmware version collection. Owner: Miguel Torres. Target: 2024-03-30.
- Revert the overlay snapshotter plugin update rolled out on 2024-03-15 to confirm regression. Owner: Lena Schmidt. Target: 2024-03-25.
- Add a node-level emergency policy to limit concurrent image pulls (leaky-bucket) for model-serving rollout jobs. Owner: oncall. Target: immediate (experiment).
- Add temporary kubelet tuning: increase eviction hard threshold for ephemeral-storage by 5% and increase kube-reserved for system slices to account for observed blocking. Owner: SRE-runbook team. Change request: SRE-4431.

Longer-term action items (>72h):
- Work with hardware vendor to validate NVMe firmware across fleet and schedule constrained firmware roll forward or decommissioning of failing devices. Owner: infra hw ops.
- Improve containerd snapshotter to use asynchronous fsync batching for large lightweight checkpoint files. Track: github PR #72 (linked). Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Add an automated detection alert for cgroupv2 io.stat time/bytes anomalies mapped to kubelet pod-start-latency. Proposed alert rule in prometheus: increase when io.stat.time_write rate spikes + pod_start_latency_95th > 800ms for >5min.
- Update node lab test harness to reproduce heavy mmap+fsync patterns and measure overlay snapshotter behavior under cgroupv2. Owner: applied-ml infra.

Notes to future on-call responders (playbook snippets):
- If you see high kubelet pod start latency with containerd snapshotter errors, prioritize disk diagnostics (iostat, dmesg, smartctl) before restarting kubelet. Restarting kubelet without addressing disk stalls will likely not fix root cause and may trigger pod churn.
- When draining, use --delete-local-data only after verifying pods do not need local NVMe state; many model-serving pods write warmed caches to local NVMe and will rebuild slowly elsewhere.
- Use our snapshot-debug.sh to capture overlay metadata; stash the tarball in S3 under s3://redwood-triage/2024-03-20-cgroupv2-throttle/ for postmortem.

Owners and stakeholders:
- Primary incident owner (oncall): Asha Patel (eng-sre)
- Hardware vendor liaison: Miguel Torres (infra)
- Container runtime owner: Lena Schmidt (serving-runtime)
- Product impact contact: Priya Nair (product-hosted-api)

Postmortem plan and required artifacts:
- Draft a short postmortem summarizing timeline, root cause hypothesis, and mitigation within 7 days. Owner: Asha. Linked ticket: SRE-4431.
- Collect the following artifacts and attach to the ticket: kubelet+containerd logs, snapshot-debug bundle, iostat outputs, SMART dumps, kernel dmesg, list of affected pod ids and node names.
- Run a canary with overlay snapshotter reverted and with artificial throttling to validate whether the revert fixes the issue.

Open questions for follow-up meeting:
- Should we implement per-node image-pull concurrency limits in kubelet or at admission controller level for heavy model deployments? Pros/cons and perf test plan.
- Is cgroupv2 io.stat granularity sufficient for robust detection or do we need kernel PSI integration into kubelet heuristics?

Related links and artifacts (copyable):
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-4431
- Snapshotter revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kubelet-ops/pull/72
- Temp artifacts S3: s3://redwood-triage/2024-03-20-cgroupv2-throttle/
- Slack thread: #sre-oncall, thread id 1589123

Quick appendix: sample diagnostic output excerpts (sanitized)

1) /proc/pressure/io at peak:
some avg10=0.93 avg60=0.71 avg300=0.34 total=12345678
full avg10=0.77 avg60=0.58 avg300=0.29 total=8765432

2) iostat snippet (impacted node):
Device        r/s   w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s  r_await  w_await  aqu-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1      30.2  560.1  1024.0  512000  0.00   0.00    5.21     1800.23  25.3   1002.14  0.86  99.9

3) containerd overlayfs EIO fragment:
Mar 20 02:12:13 node-015 containerd[1123]: time="2024-03-20T02:12:13Z" level=error msg="snapshotter failed: failed to commit: write: unexpected EOF: syscall EIO"

If you are reading this as the next on-call: add any new observations directly under a new "Updates" section at the bottom and paste relevant log snippets. We want to avoid rebuilding the same context each rotation.

-- Asha
